https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases.text: The project celebrates its 10th anniversary with new member growth and the recipients of the first-ever Community Awards at Zephyr Developer Summit in Prague Summary The Zephyr Project marks its 10th anniversary by expanding its ecosystem with seven new Silver members that bring deep expertise across the entire embedded product lifecycle. These additions strengthen Zephyr's position as a secure, vendor-neutral foundation for the next generation of connected devices and industrial automation. The community will celebrate these milestones and the recipients of the first-ever Community Awards at the upcoming Zephyr Developer Summit in Prague in October. SAN FRANCISCO , Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Zephyr® Project , an open source project at the Linux Foundation building a secure, connected and flexible real-time operating system (RTOS) for resource-constrained devices, today announced seven new Silver members: Canonical , Dojo Five , GigaDevice , Morse Micro , Northern.tech , Siemens and Space Cubics . This growth marks a decade of collaboration and commercial expansion across the embedded ecosystem. The addition of these members reflects Zephyr's growing role as a shared, vendor-neutral technology foundation. As more companies build connected, resource-constrained devices on Zephyr, the ecosystem is expanding to support the full product lifecycle, from firmware architecture, connectivity and security to testing, deployment, software updates and long-term maintenance. By bringing production experience and expertise across these areas, the new members are helping strengthen Zephyr as a reliable, portable platform that companies rely on. To recognize the people who helped build that foundation, the project introduced the Zephyr Community Awards . The awards honor developers, maintainers and community members whose technical contributions, leadership, documentation and advocacy have shaped Zephyr over the past 10 years. Winners will be announced at the Zephyr Developer Summit, taking place alongside the Open Source Summit Europe , from October 7-9 in Prague. The Zephyr Maintainers Forum will provide an additional dedicated forum for maintainers to collaborate in person on the technical and community priorities shaping the project. "Over the last decade, Zephyr has evolved to become a foundational technology that companies are depending on for the long term," said Kate Stewart, vice president of dependable embedded systems at the Linux Foundation. "New members bring investment and expertise, developers bring the experience of building real products and our maintainers turn that collaboration into technology the entire ecosystem uses. That's what has made the project successful, and what will carry it through years to come." Learn more about the Zephyr Community Awards , register for the Zephyr Developer Summit and Zephyr Maintainers Forum or learn more about the Zephyr Project here: https://www.zephyrproject.org/ . Supporting Quotes "Zephyr represents the kind of open, vendor-neutral collaboration the embedded industry needs as devices get smaller and more connected. It has become foundational infrastructure for connected devices, and Canonical wants to help shape where it goes next. Joining the Zephyr Project formalizes our conviction that a strong, open RTOS deserves direct investment. We look forward to contributing to the community building the RTOS layer that so much of the industry now relies on." – Jonathan Beri, Head of Product, IoT, Canonical "Over the past decade, Zephyr has demonstrated what embedded development can become when openness, portability and community replace fragmented approaches. Dojo Five joined the Zephyr Project because we want to strengthen that foundation and make it easier for product teams to confidently build, verify, deploy and maintain production-ready embedded systems. We look forward to contributing our practical experience in firmware architecture, security, safety, testing and modernizing embedded development while helping organizations take Zephyr-based products from initial development through dependable, long-term deployment." – Joe Schneider, Founder and CEO, Dojo Five "Open source ecosystem expansion is critical for GigaDevice's GD32 MCU global business. Joining the Zephyr Project as a Silver Member enables us to deepen community collaboration, improve native Zephyr support across our GD32 product lineup, and deliver a more streamlined development experience for worldwide IoT and industrial developers." – Vincent Li, SVP and General Manager, MCU Business Unit, GigaDevice "We're proud to join the Zephyr Project, the leading open source real time operating system for embedded platforms. Morse Micro's Wi-Fi HaLow is highly complementary to Zephyr's platform agnostic design, enabling developers to easily build secure, low power, long range connected devices." – Michael De Nil, Co-founder and CEO, Morse Micro "Zephyr has become an important foundation for the next generation of connected, resource-constrained devices, and we see a growing need to manage those devices reliably throughout their entire software lifecycle. As Mender supports software updates for Zephyr-based microcontrollers, joining the Zephyr Project is a natural step for us. We look forward to working more closely with the community and contributing our experience in robust and secure software updates to help ensure connected devices are more reliable and maintainable throughout their lifetime." – Thomas Ryd, CEO, Northern.tech "Siemens is proud to join the Zephyr Project, strengthening our clear commitment to the open-source community. As a global leader in industrial automation and software, we look forward to leveraging Zephyr's secure, scalable and modular RTOS to power our industry-grade products. By actively contributing to this vibrant ecosystem, we aim to accelerate digital transformation, ensuring our embedded solutions meet the highest standards of reliability, security and open innovation for our customers worldwide." – Dominik Tacke, Principal Key Expert, Siemens Spacecraft must deliver dependable real-time operation and remain maintainable over long product lifecycles, even as their on-board computers vary with mission needs. Zephyr provides the open, vendor-neutral foundation we need to meet these requirements without tying our software to a single hardware platform. By joining the Zephyr Project, Space Cubics looks forward to contributing our experience in radiation-tolerant computing, expanding upstream support for space-grade hardware and helping make open source software a practical foundation for missions in Earth orbit, on the Moon and beyond. – Yasushi Shoji, Co-founder and CEO, Space Cubics, Inc. About the Zephyr Project The Zephyr® Project is an open source, scalable real-time operating system (RTOS) supporting multiple hardware architectures. To learn more, please visit www.zephyrproject.org . About the Linux Foundation The Linux Foundation is the world's leading home for collaboration on open source software, hardware, standards, and data. Linux Foundation projects, including Linux, Kubernetes, Model Context Protocol (MCP), OpenChain, OpenSearch, OpenSSF, OpenStack, PyTorch, Ray, RISC-V, SPDX and Zephyr, provide the foundation for global infrastructure. The Linux Foundation is focused on leveraging best practices and addressing the needs of contributors, users, and solution providers to create sustainable models for open collaboration. For more information, please visit us at linuxfoundation.org . For a list of trademarks of The Linux Foundation, please see its trademark usage page: linuxfoundation.org/trademark-usage . https://krmg.com/2026/09/09/norway-bids-.text: News Traffic Weather On Air Dallas Cowboys on KRMG More Events Contests Podcasts Advertising Contact Us Categories Breaking News Business Contests Entertainment Green Country Local News National News News Oklahoma News Politics Sports Station Information Top Stories Uncategorized World News Home Norway bids final farewell to popular King Harald V as crowds and royals converge for his funeral World News Norway bids final farewell to popular King Harald V as crowds and royals converge for his funeral by Associated Press September 9, 2026 OSLO, Norway (AP) — Norway bade its final farewell to Harald V on Wednesday as crowds lined the streets and foreign royals and leaders converged on Oslo for the funeral of the long-serving king, who was remembered as a popular monarch with a down-to-earth touch. A 21-gun salute rang out over the capital at the start of a funeral procession from the royal palace to Oslo Cathedral. Harald’s son, new King Haakon VIII , and other senior royals walked behind the coffin, draped with the red Norwegian royal standard. Harald’s widow, Queen Sonja, and Haakon’s wife, Queen Mette-Marit, followed in a car. Norwegian officials and foreign dignitaries joined the solemn procession. They included the monarchs of Sweden, Denmark, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Monaco and Jordan. Advertisement Also present were the heir to the British throne, Prince William, and Japan’s Crown Prince Akishino, as well as political leaders from more than 20 countries, including Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. As the funeral service began, Norway came to a halt for a minute of silence. Harald, who died on Aug. 28 aged 89, was Europe’s oldest monarch and had reigned for 35 years. He modernized the royal house but refused to follow in the footsteps of other aging monarchs who recently abdicated. His son immediately became king and last week took an oath of allegiance to Norway’s constitution in parliament. The parliament's speaker, Masud Gharahkhani, said at the service that “King Harald was close to the people” and recalled that “he wasn’t afraid to meet people in his rubber boots.” He remembered Harald saying in his 2008 New Year's address: “I wish we would stop using the term ‘the weakest in society.’ In reality, some of these people are among the strongest of us all.” “He lived up to his motto: He gave his all for Norway,” Gharahkhani said. Large crowds flocked to Oslo for the funeral, and thousands stood behind barriers on streets lined with national flags. The downtown area was closed to vehicles and electric scooters, and police had instructed people not to bring bicycles, umbrellas or sharp objects. People tuned in across the country of about 5.6 million. Scores of churches, libraries, cultural centers and city halls made big screens available for the public to watch the funeral, public broadcaster NRK reported. The government said it wasn’t an official holiday, but schools and workplaces could individually opt to let students and employees watch. Ahead of the funeral, Norwegians waited patiently to file past Harald's coffin in the chapel of the royal palace. The queue was seven hours long at one point over the weekend. Over 46,000 people visited the chapel during the week it lay in state. “The love between the people and King Harald has not ended — quite the contrary,” said Bishop Olav Fykse Tveit, who led the funeral service, pointing to the tributes left outside the palace after his death. “The sea of flowers, along with the words and drawings that accompany them, speaks loudly and clearly of a heart so full that it overflows.” After the funeral, Harald's coffin was taken in a smaller procession to Akershus Fortress, where his predecessors are buried in the crypt of the palace chapel. Haakon followed with the two other Scandinavian monarchs, King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden and King Frederik X of Denmark. Among those who attended the funeral was Mette-Marit’s eldest son and Haakon's stepson, Marius Borg Høiby, who has no royal title or duties. Høiby is appealing against a rape conviction after a trial earlier this year that cast a shadow over the royal family. Norway’s monarchy traces its origins to King Harald Fairhair in the ninth century. When Norway regained its independence from Sweden in 1905, three-quarters of voters in a national plebiscite approved restoring the monarchy. The Norwegian royal house has kinfolk in other European royal families . Harald and Haakon are related to both Britain’s King Charles III and Spain’s King Felipe VI: They’re all descendants of the U.K.'s Queen Victoria, who reigned from 1837 until her death in 1901. Today, the throne's role is largely symbolic and power lies with the elected government and parliament, but the Norwegian royal family retains a role in promoting the wealthy Scandinavian nation around the world. ___ Associated Press writers Geir Moulson in Berlin, Jamey Keaten in Geneva and Claudia Ciobanu in Warsaw, Poland contributed to this report. https://breakingdefense.com/2026/10/thal.text: Thales has tested its HexaForce C2 platform that it hopes to export to Gulf nations. (Photo courtesy of Thales) BEIRUT — French aerospace and defense giant Thales is pitching its new artificial intelligence-enabled command and control system, dubbed HexaForce, as a solution specifically for the Gulf market, a top executive told Breaking Defense. “We do believe that there is an operational need and a solution based on our open standard, being able to address the sovereignty for the countries. We do believe that this solution is already fit for purpose regarding the Gulf,” Thales Vice President for Multi-Domain Operations Patrick Moreau said in an interview Tuesday. Moreau declined to comment on any discussions the company may be having with individual Middle East customers. Unveiled Sept. 17, HexaForce is designed to “accelerate decision-making and secure operational advantage at every level of command” for “NATO and allied nations,” the company’s release explains. “This solution is a data, AI-powered solution. We leverage on the AI to develop quite fast, and there is agentic and LLM [large language model] inside this solution [that] could really allow the end users, for instance, to propose targeting solution to the operator, meaning that it allows the operator to process a huge amount of data,” Moreau said. He added that HexaForce is based on open-source data, allowing users to reinforce sovereign capability within the state. This means, Moreau explained, if “you understand how it has been built and you could adapt the solution for the local needs. The [operational] data remains the property of the nation, meaning that it will remain within the country, guaranteeing the sovereignty of the solution.” Thales says the platform also covers both strategic- and tactical-level decision making. While the C2 platform has yet to be deployed in any conflict, it has been tested in military exercises like the CWIX NATO exercise that took place in June in Poland. By Breaking Defense The live-trial phases of HexaForce will forge a path for “for full-scale deployment, targeting an increase in capacity from 100 to 1,000 targets processed per day,” Thales’ release states. Regarding the possibility of coproduction of this system with Gulf states in compliance with localization efforts in the region, Moreau answered, “whenever we deploy it locally, we could rely on domestic capabilities of Thales and/or partners to develop AI-powered capability, which are much more sovereign, considered as sovereign eyes only by the country.” Gulf states like Saudi Arabia , United Arab Emirates and Qatar have stressed local production in recent years according to national mandates.
